input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I’m not sure about making calls or using the internet right now, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my phone screen. Does that mean something? I don’t remember seeing any specific error messages when I try to send a picture message—it just doesn’t go through. What should I do next?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said, and now I see the signal bars at the top again. But I tried sending a picture message, and it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try?

I do see a “5G” icon and something that looks like a little phone with some bars next to it at the top of my screen. Does that mean my mobile data is on? I’m not sure how to check the internet otherwise—should I still try to open a web page, or is the icon enough?

I checked, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s something called an MMSC URL that looks like “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right or not—does that help? I haven’t changed anything there myself.

I really don’t know how to reset those settings, and honestly, I get nervous messing with things like that. My phone is a Samsung, but I’m not sure which model exactly. Could you give me simple, step-by-step instructions? And… will this mess up anything else on my phone, like my photos or contacts? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Alright, I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings. It said they’ll reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit worried—if I restart, am I really not going to lose any of my photos or messages? I just want to be sure before I do it.
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. Also, it looks like my messaging app only has permission for the phone—does it need something else to send picture messages? What should I do next?

Alright, I went into the settings and gave the messaging app permission for both storage and SMS. I just tried sending a picture message again, and it looks like it’s finally working! Thank you so much for your help—I was really getting worried there.

Thank you so much for your patience and reassurance. I really appreciate your help walking me through everything. I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble, but for now, I’m just happy it’s working again. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you, John. I’ve found your account. To help you fix the MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks and steps on your phone.

First, can you confirm:
- Are you able to make regular calls and use mobile data (like browsing the web) on your phone right now?
- Are you seeing any error messages when trying to send MMS?

Let me know, and I’ll walk you through the next steps to resolve this.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%

I’m not sure about making calls or using the internet right now, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my phone screen. Does that mean something? I don’t remember seeing any specific error messages when I try to send a picture message—it just doesn’t go through. What should I do next?

The airplane icon means your phone is in Airplane Mode, which disables all wireless connections—including calls, mobile data, and MMS. This is likely why your picture messages aren’t going through.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon so it is no longer highlighted.

Once Airplane Mode is off, wait a few seconds for your phone to reconnect to the network. Then, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said, and now I see the signal bars at the top again. But I tried sending a picture message, and it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try?

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode. Since you now see signal bars but still can’t send picture messages, let’s check a few more things to identify the issue.

Could you please check if your mobile data is enabled? MMS requires mobile data to send and receive picture messages, even if you have a signal for calls and texts.

Here’s how you can check:
1. Look for a “4G,” “LTE,” “5G,” or similar icon near your signal bars. If you see one, mobile data is likely enabled.
2. If you don’t see any of those icons, try opening a web page in your browser (with Wi-Fi turned off) to see if you have internet access.

Let me know what you find, and I’ll guide you through the next steps!

I do see a “5G” icon and something that looks like a little phone with some bars next to it at the top of my screen. Does that mean my mobile data is on? I’m not sure how to check the internet otherwise—should I still try to open a web page, or is the icon enough?

Seeing the “5G” icon and the phone with bars at the top of your screen is a good sign—this usually means your mobile data is enabled and you have a strong connection. You don’t need to check the internet separately if those icons are present.

Since mobile data is on and you still can’t send MMS, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent MMS from working.

Could you please check your APN settings on your phone and let me know if you see anything unusual, or if you’re not sure how to check, let me know your phone’s make and model (e.g., iPhone 13, Samsung Galaxy S21), and I can guide you through the steps.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s something called an MMSC URL that looks like “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right or not—does that help? I haven’t changed anything there myself.

Thank you for checking your APN settings and sharing the details. The APN name and MMSC URL you provided look generally correct, but sometimes even a small error or a hidden issue can cause MMS problems.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to the default values, as this often resolves MMS issues. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or do you already know how to do this on your device? If you let me know your phone’s make and model, I can provide specific instructions.

I really don’t know how to reset those settings, and honestly, I get nervous messing with things like that. My phone is a Samsung, but I’m not sure which model exactly. Could you give me simple, step-by-step instructions? And… will this mess up anything else on my phone, like my photos or contacts? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Resetting your APN settings is safe and will not affect your photos, contacts, or any personal data—it only restores your network settings to their default values. This is a common troubleshooting step for fixing MMS and mobile data issues.

Here are simple, step-by-step instructions for most Samsung phones:

1. Open the **Settings** app on your phone.
2. Tap on **Connections** (or it might say **Network & Internet**).
3. Tap on **Mobile networks**.
4. Tap on **Access Point Names** or **APN**.
5. You’ll see a list of APNs. Tap the three dots in the top right corner (or “More”).
6. Select **Reset to default**.

After you reset the APN settings:
- Restart your phone (power it off, then turn it back on).

Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you need help with any of these steps or if you run into any issues!

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings. It said they’ll reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit worried—if I restart, am I really not going to lose any of my photos or messages? I just want to be sure before I do it.

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, contacts, or personal data by restarting your phone. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new network settings. It does not delete or change any of your personal files or apps.

It’s completely safe to restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works or if you need further help.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Okay, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience and for following the previous steps. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, restarted your phone, and still can’t send MMS, let’s continue troubleshooting. There are a few more things we can check:

1. Let’s make sure Wi-Fi Calling is turned off, as it can sometimes interfere with MMS on some networks.
2. We should also check that your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send and receive MMS.

Would you like step-by-step instructions for checking Wi-Fi Calling and app permissions, or do you feel comfortable checking those on your own? Let me know, and I’ll guide you through the next steps.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.

I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. Also, it looks like my messaging app only has permission for the phone—does it need something else to send picture messages? What should I do next?

Yes, your messaging app needs permission to access storage (for photos) and SMS (for sending/receiving messages) to send picture messages (MMS). If it only has permission for the phone, that could be the reason MMS isn’t working.

Here’s what you should do next:

1. Go to your phone’s **Settings**.
2. Tap on **Apps** or **Applications**.
3. Find and select your **Messaging** app.
4. Tap on **Permissions**.
5. Make sure both **Storage** and **SMS** permissions are enabled.

After granting these permissions, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if this helps or if you need more detailed instructions!

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

Alright, I went into the settings and gave the messaging app permission for both storage and SMS. I just tried sending a picture message again, and it looks like it’s finally working! Thank you so much for your help—I was really getting worried there.

I’m glad to hear that your picture messages are working now! Granting the correct permissions often resolves this type of issue. If you have any more questions or run into any other problems, feel free to reach out—I’m here to help.

Have a great day, and enjoy sending your pictures!
